title: Unicode normalization pre-tokenization for consistent billing across clients
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Background: Customers have reported apparent billing discrepancies between different clients/SDKs and between hosted vs private deployments. Investigation has shown a class of cases where semantically equivalent inputs are tokenized to different token counts because of variations in Unicode normalization, CRLF vs LF line endings, invisible characters (ZWJ/ZWSP), and emoji variation selectors. Problem: Without a canonical normalization step before tokenization, identical logical text (e.g., umlaut composed vs decomposed, NFKC compat ligatures, emoji modifier sequences) can produce different token sequences and therefore different per-token billing. This causes confused customers, meter reconciliation tickets, and difficulty asserting billing correctness across regions and SDKs. Goal: Implement a deterministic, documented pre-tokenization normalization layer in the metering pipeline and expose the normalization behavior in SDKs and docs so token accounting is consistent across clients and deployments, and retroactive audits are easier.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document a canonical normalization form (recommended: NFC for user-visible text, with optional NFKC for compatibility flows) and publish decision rationale in spec
Add normalization step in server-side ingestion and in reference client SDKs (Python/JS) so surface inputs are normalized before tokenization

Unit tests cover representative edge cases: composed vs decomposed accents, CRLF vs LF, ZWJ/ZWNJ, zero-width space insertion/removal, emoji sequences with/without variation selectors and skin-tone modifiers
Create integration tests that reproduce previously reported customer mismatches and assert token counts converge after normalization
Add a lightweight telemetry metric: fraction of requests that required normalization changes (characters modified) and downstream per-account token delta pre/post-normalization during rollout
Rollout plan with canary that applies normalization for 1% of requests, monitor customer-impact dashboards and error/complaint channels before wider rollout
Documentation updated: normalization specification, examples demonstrating identical logical inputs mapping to identical token counts, SDK changelog entries

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: NFKC may change user-visible text (ligatures, compatibility mappings) and could alter semantics. Mitigation: choose NFC by default and provide opt-in compatibility mode for customers requiring NFKC.

Risk: Applying normalization at different boundary layers (client vs server) could double-normalize if SDKs and servers both apply. Mitigation: define idempotent normalization and include header X-Text-Normalized indicating normalization version applied.

Risk: Performance overhead on high-throughput ingestion path. Mitigation: microbench normalization; use optimized ICU routines with pooling; only run normalization when input contains non-ASCII or when a quick pre-check identifies potential non-normalized sequences.

Risk: Retroactive audits may reveal token deltas that affect billing. Mitigation: during rollout, enable monitoring-only mode (compute normalized token delta but do not alter billing) for initial period and surface flagged accounts for manual review before changing billing behavior.
test_plan: Unit tests for normalization functions with extensive unicode test vectors
Integration tests exercising python/js clients and server tokenization to assert identical token counts
Regression test: replay 1M historical requests sampled from international customers and compare billed tokens pre/post normalization in shadow mode
Load test of normalization in hot path to ensure <5% CPU overhead at p95 traffic levels
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Spec and SDK opt-in release (documentation only)
Phase 1: Server-side shadow mode (compute normalized token count, do not change billing) for 1% of traffic for 72h
Phase 2: Increase shadow to 10% and notify top 100 customers in affected regions
Phase 3: Canary apply normalization for 1% of traffic with billing enabled for canary cohort; monitor for anomalies 7 days
Phase 4: Full rollout with header X-Text-Normalized and version, then 30-day audit window
monitoring: Alert: if >0.5% of active customers show >10% sustained token increase after normalization during canary
